The Brick under Amalthea

Buttons

Amalthea names the Brick's buttons by what they do. The same names are used throughout this manual.

"Hold" means 0.8 s unless stated otherwise. A held button acts once; letting it go does not act again.

Starting, leaving and switching off

Power on: after the boot logo, the Amalthea home screen offers TRACKER, FX and LIFEBLOOD. Choose one with the cross and press Enter. The battery charge is shown top right (red at 15 % or less, a bolt while charging).

Every appliance starts blank and stopped. Nothing is recalled automatically and nothing is saved behind your back: you load and save sessions yourself, from the bank pages.

To leave an appliance, hold FUNC first, then also hold Shift. (The reverse order does nothing.) A prompt asks CANCEL / OK; OK asks SAVE BEFORE EXIT?, NO / YES. YES saves to the loaded session slot (or the selected one) and returns home; NO discards the workspace and returns home.

To switch off, hold Power about a second and release it. POWER OFF? starts on NO; left/up selects YES, right/down NO; a short press of Power confirms. The prompt warns when there are unsaved changes. A save already in progress finishes before the Brick shuts down.

Volume and output

The volume keys set the output level; a bar shows it for 1.5 s in every appliance. Output goes to the headphone jack and the speaker as on the stock system.

USB audio out. While the USB-C port is not hosting an FM-1 (that is, outside FX and LIFEBLOOD's capture), the Brick presents itself to a connected computer or phone as a class-compliant audio input, Amalthea Audio (stereo, 44.1 kHz, 16-bit): record the instrument's mix with any audio software, no driver needed. It carries the mix before the volume keys, like a line output.

TRACKER

A twelve-track generative tracker. Each track is a pattern of up to 16 steps in five columns, each column with its own length, clock and direction; each track plays one of twelve synthesis engines through two insert effects and the master chain.

The pattern page

The page shows the current track (its number large, top right, in the track's colour), 16 rows (or 8 larger rows) and five columns:

ColumnHolds
NOTEA pitch (in the session's scale), OFF or TIE; plus length, condition, pan, volume and five sends
MODEmpty (---), an OFFSET for that row's note (+02) or a TRANSPOSE from that row on (T+2)
INSTThe instrument slot for that row (-- follows the track's instrument)
FX1 / FX2An insert effect and its dry/wet mix, with a LENGTH in steps and a condition

While you edit a NOTE, every change is auditioned at once, also while stopped or on a muted track; nothing is stored until Enter. FUNC + short X on INST plays the track's instrument on the scale's root, octave 4.

NOTE tabs: VALUE, LENGTH, CONDITION, PAN, VOLUME and the five sends (DELAY, REVERB, ABRASION, CORROSION, MODULATION). Left restores the track's own value (inheritance); right copies the track value as an explicit override. Step volume is relative to the track fader.

FX tabs: DRY/WET MIX (0 % dry, 100 % fully processed; a newly chosen effect starts at 50 %), LENGTH (1–64 steps: the effect stays on its slot over the following rows, empty rows keep it running, a new effect row replaces it) and CONDITION. Effects with memory (reverbs, delays, granular, resonators) ring out on their own when they end or are replaced. No effect can feed itself into a runaway: every insert stays within reach of a fading memory of its input, so tails always die away.

Conditions A:B make an event act on cycle A of every B cycles of its own column, from 1:1 to 8:8 (36 choices). A NOTE condition gates the note; INST chooses the slot or the track default; an inactive FX row bypasses the slot; an inactive OFFSET adds nothing, and an inactive TRANSPOSE leaves the transposition as it was on that cycle.

MOD. Every MOD cell starts empty. An OFFSET shifts only its own row's note. A TRANSPOSE shifts every note from its row to the end of the MOD column's cycle, or until the next TRANSPOSE (T+0 returns to the written notes); offsets are added on top, so +02 under T+1 plays three semitones up. Each MOD cycle starts untransposed: a TRANSPOSE on step 1 transposes the whole sequence, one on step 9 only what follows it, and a TRANSPOSE with condition 1:2 transposes every other cycle while the others play as written. Up / down on an empty cell makes an OFFSET. Sessions from before build 38 load their +00 cells as empty.

Drawing at random

X is the generator, everywhere in the Tracker.

ToDo this
Randomizer options for this column (MODE, DENSITY)Tap X; tap again to return
Draw the columnHold X
Draw NOTE with conditions, pan, volume and sendsShift + hold X on NOTE
New sound for the track's instrument (written on every INST row)Hold X on INST; an overlay names it
Random instrument slots per stepShift + hold X on INST
A variation of each row's instrument (pitch kept)FUNC + hold X on INST
Draw the FX column: effects, mixes and their parametersHold X on FX1 / FX2
The same, with positive trigger conditionsShift + hold X on FX1 / FX2
While editing a cell: new value for the shown tab onlyTap X (auditioned; Enter keeps it)
While editing: that tab over the whole columnShift + hold X
While editing an FX cell: new parameters / new effectHold X / Shift + hold X

MODE is RANDOM (each generator places the events) or EUCLIDEAN (events spread as evenly as possible over the column's steps, at a random rotation). DENSITY (left/right, Shift for ×10) is the exact share of active steps that receive an event; 45 % to begin with. Both are remembered per track and column and saved with patterns.

The NOTE generator draws an idiom (ostinato, pedal point, drone, walk, lament, stab, call and answer, arpeggio, spiral), a rhythm model (euclidean, metric, offbeat, cluster, scatter, anchored) and a register, always in the session's root and scale. On a PERC track it writes a drum pattern on the kit's note map; on an FM DRUM track a one-voice rhythm around the recipe's pitch. Each boot starts from fresh entropy: draws never repeat between sessions.

Track settings (B)

Up / down selects a row, left / right changes it, F1 / F2 switches tracks.

  • LENGTH 1–16 steps (shortening keeps the hidden notes).
  • CLOCK 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1×, 2×, 4× of the session's sixteenth-note clock.
  • DIRECTION: forward, reverse, ping-pong, pendulum, odd-even, rocking, cascade, pairs, blocks reverse, blocks retro, converge, diverge, double, stride, drunk, meander, shuffle, random, fragments.
  • INSTRUMENT (the default slot, 1–12) and ENGINE (replace that slot's engine on this track).
  • VOLUME, PAN and the sends in chain order: ABRASION, CORROSION, MODULATION, DELAY, REVERB.
  • Three macro profiles (ABRASION, CORROSION, MODULATION): SOURCE MASTER follows the shared master settings; editing makes a local TRACK profile; left on SOURCE returns to MASTER.

Column settings (A)

LENGTH, CLOCK and DIRECTION for the selected column. Each starts at TRACK (following the track); an explicit value overrides it for that column only. Columns with the same length, rate and direction stay in step.

Instruments

Each track has its own twelve instrument slots, one engine each; editing a sound on one track never changes another track.

Row variations. FUNC + hold X on INST gives every row that holds an instrument its own variation of that instrument's sound: the same family, with its timbre, filter, envelopes and modulation and effect amounts redrawn for that row. Pitch, tuning, detune, FM ratios, glide, pitch envelopes and modulation, drum tuning and the output level never change, so the notes play exactly as written. A small square after the slot number marks a varied row. With rows selected (FUNC + F1 / F2) only those rows vary; while editing an INST cell, only that row. A track holds up to 16 distinct variations (later rows of a longer column reuse their instrument's). Undo restores; hold X on INST draws a new sound and clears the column's variations; ERASE or another instrument clears a row's. Variations are saved with sessions and patterns.

SlotEngineCharacter
01VAPAnalogue-style voice: 18 families (sub pressure, EBM bass, acid wound, mourning pad, noise wall, impact ...)
02PERCDrum kits in five characters (EBM, industrial, rhythmic noise, ritual, broken)
03CHIP12 families: crush bass, zap hit, LFSR storm, dead bell ...
04FIBERThe Fiber firmware's engine: experimental, ambient and open patches

A blank session starts every track on a drawn patch. Engine details.

Master effects (Y)

F1 / F2 chooses the module; up / down a parameter; left / right changes it (Shift for larger steps). The chain is ABRASION (band-weighted drive, clipping, folding) → CORROSION (bit-depth and sample-rate reduction) → MODULATION (flanger and eight-stage phaser) → COMPRESSOR → DELAY → REVERB → OUTPUT with a stereo-linked limiter. Each track sends into each bus; every module has a mix. Values are shown in real units (Hz, ms, dB, ratio, note divisions). Tails ring out after Stop.

Mixer (FUNC + Bank)

Two pages of six channels (F1 / F2): level, meters, mute and solo. Enter begins and commits an edit; volume uses up / down, mute and solo either axis. Several solos may be on; mute wins.

Patterns and sessions

Bank opens the 8 × 4 bank of 32 patterns of the current session; Shift + Bank the 8 × 8 bank of 64 sessions.

ToDo this
Select a slotCross
Load itTap Bank
Save into itHold Bank 0.8 s
Its settings: tempo, scale, root note, switch quantizeEnter (A returns)

+ marks a saved slot, ! a damaged one; the loaded slot is filled blue. A pattern holds everything about the twelve tracks; tempo, scale and root default to the session's. While playing, a pattern load waits (amber NEXT) until the end of the current loop of the longest or shortest track (SWITCH QUANTIZE). In the settings, START puts a value in edit mode, and the die beside SCALE / ROOT NOTE rolls a new pair from 38 scales. A session holds its 32 patterns, its working state and defaults. Saving is atomic and checked; nothing is ever written except when you save.

Dashboard (Shift + Back)

Five tiles: TRACK, MIXER, MASTER FX, INSERT FX and DEVICE. INSERT FX lists the processors: switching one off bypasses it on every track (without deleting it) and keeps it out of the draws. DEVICE sets the screen brightness. Both are device preferences, kept apart from sessions.

FX

A twelve-slot effect rack for an M-VAVE FM-1. The Brick hosts the FM-1 over USB, takes its separate tracks and runs each through two insert slots, every slot with its own 16-step sequencer of parameter locks.

Connecting the FM-1

The Brick has one USB-C port. Open FX first, with the computer (if any) still connected; the screen says USB: UNPLUG LAPTOP. Unplug it: after three seconds the port switches to host mode and powers the FM-1. Connect the FM-1 (after five seconds). To reconnect a computer, leave FX first (FUNC then Shift).

Each FM-1 firmware gives its own strips: Bigorna, Tonitor and Lilliput send six mono tracks, Norilsk three; a firmware in stereo mode gives one stereo strip. MIDI clock from the FM-1 (Bigorna sends it) drives tempo and transport; without it, the FX session tempo and Play are used.

Slot sequencer

Two rows of eight steps; the lit step follows playback.

ToDo this
Parameter locks of a stepEnter on the step; up / down selects, left / right sets
Return a locked parameter to the defaultShift + left
Slot default parametersB; F1 / F2 pages them
LENGTH, CLOCK, TEMPO, DIRECTION, SEQUENCER on/offA
DENSITY and COMPLEXITYY (or tap X)
Generate triggers and locksHold X

While the transport runs, a sequenced slot is heard only on triggered steps; empty steps pass dry. Stopped, or with SEQUENCER OFF, it processes continuously. COMPLEXITY 0 gives every generated step the same random setting, 100 every step its own. TEMPO per slot follows the session, or 30–300 BPM; external clock overrides it.

LIFEBLOOD

The FM-1's audio, through a generated network of the same effects, drawn as a living field: circular nodes, vessels between them and corpuscles travelling along the flow. It starts with IN joined straight to OUT.

ControlOn the fieldOn a node's parameters
XGrow a new network from the session's CHARACTERA new effect for this node
YNew parameters for every nodeNew parameters for this node
ARewire: new vessels, same nodes and parametersBack to the field
BStart / stop angiogenesisBack to the field
CrossNearest node in that directionUp / down parameter, left / right value (Shift ×10)
F1 / F2Previous / next node in flow orderPrevious / next page
EnterOpen the node—
PlayBypass: crossfade to the dry input and backsame
Bank / Shift + BankSnapshots (32) / sessions (64)same
Shift + ASession settingssame

Session settings: TEMPO (while the FM-1's clock is locked it shows EXT and the FM-1's tempo, and cannot be dialled); PATH, ABSTRACT (textures, spaces, colour) or RHYTHMIC (cuts, gates, clockable textures, everything synced and at least 72 % wet); CHARACTER, the recipe within the path (ANY; DRIFT, GRIT, SPACE, BLOOM; PULSE, CUT, GATE, MAYHEM, INDUSTRIAL); NODES, the largest network (3–7); GROWTH, the angiogenesis rate (6–120 mutations a minute); MIX, the network's wet share.

Angiogenesis: nodes drift; one mutation at a time a vessel is cut or sprouts, a node buds or is absorbed, or a node redraws its parameters. Vessels fade in and out over 120 ms; a new network crossfades from the old over half a second, letting its tails ring. Networks are always feed-forward (no feedback loops) and stay within the Brick's CPU budget.

With a multitrack firmware, each FM-1 track is its own IN, numbered down the left edge; only tracks heard in the last 30 seconds are routed, and about a third pass straight to OUT. Each track sits where the FM-1 pans it, through the network or straight to OUT: the FM-1 sends each track's pan as CC 10 on MIDI channels 1–6 (BIGORNA from build 121, in USB TRACKS mode). A track whose pan has not arrived is centred. Every insert, and the whole network, is loudness-matched to its input: engaging it changes the sound, not the level.

Effects

The same inserts serve every instrument: Tracker FX columns, FX slots and LIFEBLOOD nodes. Every parameter is shown in its real unit.

  • Drive and destruction: DISTORTION, SATURATION, OVERDRIVE, FUZZ, RECTIFY, DIODE, RAT DRIVE, WAVEFOLD, AMP SIMULATOR, BIZTORTION, FRACTURE 2, CRAZY IVAN, BITMURDERER, BITCRUSH, RATE REDUCE, LO-FI, CRUSHCLONE, CYANIDE, POLARIZER, ANGR, MULTIBAND DIST, DISINTEGRATE, BITGLITTER, PAFNUTY.
  • Filters and colour: LOWPASS, HIGHPASS, MULTIMODE FILTER, FREQUALIZER, COMBULATOR, RESONATOR, REZ SYNTH.
  • Time and space: QDELAY, CHOWMATRIX, CLOUDSEED SPACE, CLOUDS GRANULAR, RINGS, BEADS, SOFTCUT, TRANSVERB.
  • Motion: TREMOLO, PAN, ROTOR, FLANGER, PHASER, TREMOSQUARE, GATE SHAPER, CHOPPR, RING MOD, FREQ SHIFTER, WARPS.
  • Cuts, repeats and glitches: STUTTER, OOPS, BUFFER OVERRIDE, LIVECUT, SUPATRIGGA, BEAT REPEAT, TIME SHAPER, JUMBLR, SCRUBBY, GLITCHLETS, SKIDDER, GLITCHSHIFTER, PITCHNASTY, AMALGAM, GEOMETER, REPSYCHO.
  • Spectral and voices: BROKENFFT, TREEMONSTER, SMR, VOCODER, MDA VOCODER, TALKBOX.
  • RANDOM: a different effect each time it is drawn.

Rhythmic effects follow the FM-1's MIDI clock or the session tempo and realign on Start. Their sources, licences and adaptations: native effects, ported inserts, effects and references.

Updating, recovery and going back to stock

  • Update: run the installer of a newer release while Amalthea is on the home screen. It copies your sessions to the computer first.
  • Sessions on the computer: they live on the Brick in /mnt/UDISK/tracker-linux (session-slots/, fx-session-slots/, lifeblood-session-slots/). The installer copies them on every update; you can also adb pull /mnt/UDISK/tracker-linux at any time.
  • Recovery: if an installation is interrupted, the Brick's boot manager never boots a half-written system: it stays in a RAM recovery shell reachable over USB (ADB). Run the installer again to finish, or the restore script.
  • Stock: restore.sh / restore.bat writes back the stock backup the installer took.
